state.title: include/fmt/format.h

part.text: The bug is in the `exp > 0` branch of `write_decimal` (include/fmt/format.h:2651): the size reserves `count_separators(significand_size)` separators, but `write_significand` only applies grouping to the integer part (`integral_size = exp`). For e.g. `2194.139` (significand `2194139`), it reserves 2 separators while only 1 is written, padding by one extra space — so every value with a nonzero integer part gets one space too many, and values like `0.295` (which take the `0.xxx` path with no grouping) end up misaligned relative to them.
Now let me verify with a reproduction program and run the test suite:

part.text:
Fixed in include/fmt/format.h:2651.

**Root cause:** In the fixed-notation branch for `12.34`-style values (`exp > 0`, i.e. significand spans the decimal point), the output size reserved `count_separators(significand_size)` thousands separators — counting separators over *all* digits including the fractional part — but `write_significand` only applies grouping to the integer part (`integral_size = exp`). For `2194.139` (significand `2194139`), 2 separators were reserved while only 1 ("2,194") was written, padding every such value one space too wide. Values like `0.295` (integer part zero) take the `0.xxx` path with no grouping, so they stayed correctly sized — hence the misalignment relative to the others.

**Fix:** Reserve `count_separators(exp)` instead, matching the `exponent >= 0` branch which already does this correctly.

Verified with a grouped-locale repro (all outputs now exactly width 19) and the full test suite: 20/20 tests pass.
